paper.citation: Wang, L., Zhang, Y., Richardson, T. S., and Robins, J. M. (2021). Estimation of local treatment effects under the binary instrumental variable model. Biometrika 108(4), 881-894. DOI 10.1093/biomet/asab003.
paper.source_locator: Read version: arXiv:2007.14458v2, 22 March 2022; Section 3 Theorem 1 definitions, Section 5 numerical DGP and Table 2 alpha1 target; Supplement S1 equations S4-S5 inverse observed law. Published DOI metadata checked separately; no author code used or commit applicable.

mechanism.name: Binary IV: congenial complier risk difference and odds-product model

generation_equations.label: Principal strata
generation_equations.expression: q=expit(-0.4+0.8*x); P(CO|x)=q; P(AT|x)=(1-q)*q; P(NT|x)=(1-q)^2; D=Z on CO, D=1 on AT, D=0 on NT.

generation_equations.label: Complier outcome probabilities
generation_equations.expression: delta=tanh(-x); OP=exp(-0.4+x); f1=f0+delta; f0*f1/((1-f0)*(1-f1))=OP; f0 in [max(0,-delta),min(1,1-delta)].

generation_equations.label: Observed outcome
generation_equations.expression: Y|CO,D,x~Bernoulli(fD); Y|AT,x~Bernoulli(q); Y|NT,x~Bernoulli(q). Only X,Z,D,Y are returned.

sampling.dependence: iid individuals; principal stratum and outcome depend on X; Z independent of stratum and potential outcomes conditional on X

assumptions: iid individuals, consistency and no interference
Binary Z conditionally independent of potential treatments and outcomes given observed X; exclusion
Monotonicity D(1)>=D(0); source principal-stratum model includes no defiers
Instrument overlap and positive complier probability for all x in [-1,1]
Correct conditional LATE tanh model identifies its coefficient over nondegenerate X support

properties.notes: X~Uniform(-1,1); logistic instrument/stratum functions, tanh conditional LATE and exponential odds product. Treatment effect varies with X without an explicit product term in a structural linear outcome equation.

estimand.name: alpha1
estimand.definition: Slope coefficient alpha1 in E[Y(1)-Y(0)|D(1)>D(0),X=x]=tanh(alpha0+alpha1*x). Target population is the complier stratum conditional on x; scalar alpha1=-1 is explicitly reported in source Table 2. It is a curve coefficient, not marginal LATE or ATE.

truth.expression: Slope coefficient alpha1 in E[Y(1)-Y(0)|D(1)>D(0),X=x]=tanh(alpha0+alpha1*x). Target population is the complier stratum conditional on x; scalar alpha1=-1 is explicitly reported in source Table 2. It is a curve coefficient, not marginal LATE or ATE.
truth.derivation: Source alpha1=-1; independently reconstruct conditional Wald risks from eight probability cells, invert tanh and regress the resulting population linear predictor on x.

adaptations: Implement additive-LATE branch only, using exactly the source numerical constants; do not count estimator misspecification as different data laws.
Expose the source-reported scalar coefficient alpha1=-1 in the conditional LATE tanh(alpha0+alpha1*x), rather than invent a fixed-covariate or averaged target.

Independently written NumPy observed-law sampler; numerically solve the odds-product equation by bounded bisection, including OP=1, instead of cancellation-prone closed form. Seed-level author-code equivalence not claimed.
Omit fitting, bootstrap, replications and analyst-only misspecified covariates; accept caller n and seed.
